blocks.value: Bollinger Bands help traders understand whether a stock is trading unusually high or unusually low compared to its recent average.
Imagine This: A balloon expands and shrinks depending on the air inside it. Similarly, Bollinger Bands widen when the market becomes more volatile and narrow when prices become calm.
Bollinger Bands consist of three lines: a middle Moving Average, an Upper Band and a Lower Band.
When prices repeatedly touch the upper band, the stock may be trading strongly. When they approach the lower band, it may indicate weakness or a possible reversal.
⚠️ Touching a Bollinger Band does not automatically mean the price will reverse.
Bollinger Bands work best when combined with trend analysis and RSI.
